name: Željana Zovko - Draft Council decision
part_text:
The European Parliament agrees to a trade deal between the European Union and Norway. The deal updates import limits, called tariff rate quotas, that the EU set at the World Trade Organization. These limits had to be split when the United Kingdom left the EU. Talks with other trading partners led the EU to change the volumes for three products: two in pig meat and one in skimmed-milk powder. Norway accepted these changes. Parliament's consent lets the Council conclude the deal.

- The EU changes import volumes for two pig meat quotas and one skimmed-milk powder quota.
- It affects EU and Norwegian traders in these farm products.
- Once the Council adopts it, the agreement can enter into force.
